title: Anime Head Construction: Front View
summary: Build a balanced front-view head from simple guides before drawing features. This first exercise values clear construction over a finished picture.

steps.title: 1. Draw the cranial circle
steps.explanation: Draw a light circle for the main skull mass. It does not need to be mechanically perfect: keep the stroke loose and make two or three passes if needed. Leave space below it for the jaw.

steps.title: 2. Add the vertical centerline
steps.explanation: Draw a straight vertical guide through the circle. In a front view it divides the head into left and right halves and continues down to the chin. If it leans, the face will read as turned or tilted.

steps.title: 3. Place the eye-line
steps.explanation: Draw a horizontal guide through the center of the cranial circle. Keep it perpendicular to the centerline. This is a construction guide for consistent feature placement, not the final eye shape.

steps.title: 4. Construct the jaw and chin
steps.explanation: From both lower sides of the circle, taper two jaw lines toward a short, rounded chin on the centerline. Mirror the large angles first; subtle asymmetry can be added deliberately later.

steps.title: 5. Check before adding features
steps.explanation: Compare the left and right silhouette, confirm that the chin meets the centerline, and check that the eye-line is level. Correct the guides now—features placed on a distorted construction inherit the distortion.

completion_criteria: A visible cranial circle is present.
The centerline passes through the circle and reaches the chin.
The eye-line crosses the centerline approximately at a right angle.
Both jaw sides connect the cranial mass to a centered chin.
Construction remains visible; facial details are optional for this attempt.
practice_prompt: Create three constructions. Draw the first slowly, the second with fewer corrective strokes, and the third from memory. Do not trace the previous attempt.
